nodes.label: Hybrid Live/Historical Data Approach
nodes.rationale: Live sessions use OpenF1 polling (1-5s), historical analysis uses Fast-F1 pre-computed data served via own API; cache duration is tiered by volatility (telemetry 1-2s live, historical indefinite).

nodes.label: Next.js Live Data Proxy Routes
nodes.rationale: API routes proxy OpenF1 to add caching and rate limiting between the polling client and the public API.

nodes.label: Timing Tower Component Spec
nodes.rationale: Timing tower columns adapt per session type: mini-sectors and Q1/Q2/Q3 columns only in practice/qualifying, interval/pit-stop columns only in sprint/race.

nodes.label: Tauri Desktop App Approach
nodes.rationale: Tauri chosen over Electron for ~10-20MB bundles vs 150MB+, lower memory via native webview, faster startup, and stronger isolation; Electron only if Node.js native modules or specific Chromium features are required. Requires converting Next.js to static export and moving API routes client-side or to Rust commands.

nodes.label: Modular F1 Data Architecture
nodes.rationale: F1 data hardcoded in TypeScript required code changes for every update; the hybrid replaces it with API-driven live data (OpenF1/Ergast), git-versioned JSON for manual circuit visuals and reference data, and surgical override files for API corrections.

nodes.label: Override Merging Pattern
nodes.rationale: API data stays the base; usually-empty override JSON files specify only fields needing correction and are merged surgically, with static fallback JSON served (X-Data-Source: fallback) when the API fails, so corrections never fork the dataset.

nodes.label: Session-Aware Polling
nodes.rationale: Polling interval depends on session type and live status: race/sprint 1.5s because position changes are critical, qualifying 2s for lap times, practice/testing 5s to save resources, 60s when not live.

nodes.label: Circuit Data JSON Schema
nodes.rationale: One JSON file per circuit gives clean diffs and easy editing; 0-1 position values along the track path work with existing getPointAtLength() visualization logic.

nodes.label: Unified Motorsport Calendar
nodes.rationale: Separate JSON files per series organized by category (formula/endurance/rally/motorcycle/stock/touring) under one shared MotorsportEvent schema, so F1, WEC, WRC, MotoGP and others render in one filterable calendar and the Season panel migrates to the same structure.

nodes.label: calendarStore (Zustand)
nodes.rationale: Series filter selection persists to localStorage so include/exclude choices survive reloads.
